name: Xero
tagline: Cloud accounting, invoicing, bank reconciliation, payroll add-ons, and reporting

pricing.notes: Official US pricing checked 2026-07-30; Early listed at $25/month after promotional discounts, with higher Growing/Established tiers.

tiers.name: Early
tiers.limits: 20 invoices/quotes per month; 5 bills per month; 30-day cash-flow forecast

tiers.name: Growing
tiers.limits: Unlimited invoices, quotes, and bills; 60-day cash-flow forecast

tiers.name: Established
tiers.limits: Unlimited invoices and bills; 180-day forecast; multi-currency, projects, and expenses

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; 1-month free trial or temporary promotional discount
pricing.billingTerms: monthly only; no annual plan; one month's notice to cancel and downgrade changes can be delayed by one month
pricing.hiddenCosts: Non-standard bill-payment methods and optional Inventory Plus cost extra. The current 90%-off introductory offer is temporary; list prices remain $25/$55/$90 through September 30, 2026.

verdictSummary: Invoices and reports are buildable, but Xero's real product is bank feeds, accounting workflows, accountant collaboration, compliance expectations, integrations, and trust.
coreLoopDIY: Build simple bookkeeping with invoices, expenses, CSV imports, chart of accounts, and reports for personal/internal use.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because businesses need dependable books, not just a ledger UI.

priorArt.name: Odoo
priorArt.desc: Open-source business suite with accounting modules; heavier than a solo DIY clone.

alternatives.name: ERPNext
alternatives.desc: Accounting, invoices, reconciliation, inventory and payroll in one free ERP; the server becomes another account to reconcile.

facts.install: Managed Frappe Cloud signup, or the supported Frappe Docker/Bench deployment
facts.dataFormat: Self-hosted companies live in MariaDB site databases with site files and attachments on the server; managed-hosting data lives in the selected Frappe Cloud site.
facts.gapVsPaid: ERPNext is an ERP deployment rather than a ready-made small-business service and lacks Xero's broad live-bank, payment, accountant, payroll, and app-marketplace integrations out of the box.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting is an ERP deployment rather than a desktop install: Docker or Bench, MariaDB, Redis, workers, a reverse proxy, backups, upgrades, and country-specific accounting setup.

alternatives.name: Manager Desktop
alternatives.desc: A full local ledger with invoices and reconciliation; there is no shared cloud unless you provide one.

facts.install: Native desktop installer for Windows, macOS, or Linux
facts.dataFormat: Each business is stored in a local .manager file backed by SQLite, including its accounting records and attached documents; the user chooses and backs up that file.
facts.gapVsPaid: Manager Desktop's local company file cannot match Xero's real-time multi-user collaboration, automatic bank feeds, mobile capture, payroll links, and accountant ecosystem.

alternatives.name: Bigcapital
alternatives.desc: Modern double-entry books, expenses and inventory in Docker; live bank feeds are not magically free.

facts.install: Official server setup script and Docker-based deployment
facts.dataFormat: Books, contacts, invoices, bills, inventory, and settings live in the deployment's MariaDB database, with generated files and attachments on configured server storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Bigcapital lacks Xero's mature bank-feed network, payment and payroll integrations, accountant tools, and low-maintenance hosted operation.
facts.setupBlocker: It needs a Linux server, Docker, DNS and HTTPS, database and mail configuration, backups, and upgrades; the hosted product is not the indefinitely free path.

alternatives.name: LedgerSMB
alternatives.desc: Serious accounting, invoicing, stock and reports; the interface is less polished and more interested in balancing.

facts.install: Docker Compose is the shortest documented path; packages and manual Perl installation also exist
facts.dataFormat: Companies and accounting records live in PostgreSQL databases; uploaded or generated documents live in the configured document store or server volumes.
facts.gapVsPaid: LedgerSMB is less polished and far less integrated than Xero for bank feeds, payments, payroll, mobile work, app connections, and accountant collaboration.
facts.setupBlocker: The first obstacle is a real web stack, Docker, PostgreSQL, administrator credentials, a reverse proxy and TLS for internet use, plus backups and upgrades.

alternatives.name: Frappe Books
alternatives.desc: Offline invoices, bills, payments and reports with a real ledger; multi-user cloud work is absent.

facts.install: Native desktop installer; Homebrew and Flatpak paths are also published
facts.dataFormat: Each company is a local SQLite .db file selected by the user, with its ledger, invoices, bills, and related records in that file.
facts.gapVsPaid: Frappe Books is a local SQLite desktop ledger, so it gives up Xero's shared cloud workspace, managed bank feeds, payroll links, payment network, and accountant access.

alternatives.name: Odoo Accounting (One App Free)
alternatives.desc: A hosted accounting app for zero dollars; add another unrelated Odoo app and the meter starts.

facts.install: Create an Odoo Online database and select Accounting as the single free app
facts.dataFormat: Accounting records and attachments live in the Odoo Online database and filestore operated by Odoo; the internal storage format is not exposed to the hosted user.
facts.gapVsPaid: The one-app-free plan is usable accounting, but Xero's bank connections and specialist ecosystem are broader, and adding a separate Odoo app can turn the database into a paid subscription.
facts.setupBlocker: The first obstacle is configuring the correct country localization, chart of accounts, taxes, journals, and bank import; installing any additional priced Odoo app ends One App Free eligibility.

alternatives.name: Dolibarr
alternatives.desc: Invoices, banks, stock and double-entry accounting in one practical suite; native payroll is not included.

facts.install: DoliWamp, DoliDeb, DoliRPM, Docker, or a conventional PHP web-server installation
facts.dataFormat: Business records live in MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL, while uploaded and generated documents live in Dolibarr's documents directory or mounted volume.
facts.gapVsPaid: Dolibarr requires more administration and lacks Xero's polished automatic bank reconciliation, payment and payroll integrations, mobile capture, and accountant network.
facts.setupBlocker: A packaged desktop-style installer exists on some platforms, but a durable deployment still needs a web server or Docker, database, HTTPS, backups, updates, and localization.

alternatives.name: GnuCash
alternatives.desc: Desktop double-entry books, invoicing and reports; bank automation and collaboration are the losses.

facts.install: Native desktop installer or operating-system package
facts.dataFormat: The default book is a local compressed XML .gnucash file; SQLite, MySQL, and PostgreSQL backends are optional, but the documentation warns that database storage does not make GnuCash a true multi-user application.
facts.gapVsPaid: GnuCash is a desktop ledger rather than a collaborative cloud service and has no comparable managed bank-feed, payroll, payments, mobile, or accountant ecosystem.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Akaunting
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free base is single-entry unless you buy the Double-Entry app, and the repo is BSL rather than open source.

notes: Another structural no due regulatory/financial integrations.
prompt:
Build me a freelancer bookkeeping app covering the personal slice of Xero:
invoices, expenses, and quarterly reports. Requirements:

- A local web app: Node + Express + better-sqlite3; income and expense entries
  with date, amount, category, client, and an attached receipt file.
- CSV import from my bank's export, plus a rules table (description pattern to
  category) so repeat transactions auto-categorize.
- Invoices numbered sequentially, rendered to PDF with pdfkit, one paid/unpaid
  flag. Nothing more.
- Reports: quarterly income, expenses by category, and a one-page cash P&L I
  can print for my accountant.
- Binds to localhost only, no accounts, no telemetry; write a nightly copy of
  the SQLite file to a dated backup.
- Out of scope: bank feeds, reconciliation, payroll, tax filing, and audit
  history. Do not build any of them; if I need real accounting, Odoo or
  Invoice Ninja is the honest route.
- README: state that this is a ledger for staying organized between real tools,
  not accounting. Xero's product is bank feeds, reconciliation, and books an
  accountant will accept, and no one should sign off these numbers unchecked.
